source_caption:
One of the most emotionally devastating sequences in Interstellar occurs when Cooper returns from Miller’s planet and must catch up on 23 years of accumulated video messages from his children, culminating in the heartbreaking appearance of a now-adult Murph (Jessica Chastain). To ensure the rawest possible emotional reaction, director Christopher Nolan completely withheld the pre-recorded footage from Matthew McConaughey prior to filming. When McConaughey sat down in front of the monitor on set, it was his very first time seeing or hearing the videos, including Chastain’s devastating delivery of the line, “Today is my birthday... and it’s a special one because you told me you’d be back by the time I was the same age that you were when you left.” The uncontrollable sobbing and visceral grief captured on screen was McConaughey’s genuine, unscripted reaction caught perfectly on the very first take.

Interstellar (2014), directed by Christopher Nolan, starring Matthew McConaughey, Anne Hathaway, Jessica Chastain, Michael Caine. As Earth faces a devastating global blight and inevitable extinction, a former NASA pilot leads a desperate, last-ditch mission through a newly discovered wormhole to find a habitable new home for humanity among the stars.

source_details.synopsis: Interstellar is a 2014 epic science fiction drama film directed by Christopher Nolan, who co-wrote the screenplay with his brother, Jonathan Nolan. It features an ensemble cast led by Matthew McConaughey, Anne Hathaway, Jessica Chastain, Bill Irwin, Ellen Burstyn, and Michael Caine. Set in a dystopian future where Earth is suffering from catastrophic blight and famine, the film follows a group of astronauts who travel through space in search of a new home for humanity. The film began development in 2006 from a treatment by producer Lynda Obst and theoretical physicist Kip Thorne, and was originally set to be directed by Steven Spielberg.
